fixes.text: The front is still the quiet half: in front34, crop-nose and top, the bonnet around the yellow 451 window and the black duct shows only thin, dim brown stair lines, and the bumper corners are mostly black. This is the execution the owner flagged. On the doors and haunch (side_l, side_r) and over the roof (top), the linework reads as one even pixel maze or camo: one ink, one cell size, one line weight. None of the SPIRIT structure shows: no distinct panels with black gutters between them, no nested frames or border rows, no dim #6B3528 panels, and no yellow inner lines at nose and tail. Make the separate panels and at least a second line weight visible at 10 m.

The sponsor layer is thin. Each side has about six small icon marks, under the number and behind the door, and the black sill from the door shut line to the rear wheel, below the sim's light panel, is a plain field (side_l, side_r). The nose corners and rear bumper carry no visible roster marks (front34, rear34). That is well short of the brief's 12-16 small sponsors.

answers.note: The nose now has its own heat (nose_heat 1.0 over nose_w 0.4 u), so the bonnet, fender noses and front fenders draw solid and hot terracotta panels like the engine cover; the bonnet vent, both bumper corners and the rear face carry a full-cell terracotta stair tile instead of round 1's dim half-cell one, so the vent no longer merges with the black 451 window; nose panels carry yellow inner lines. Evidence: sim 20261021-234724 front34.png (crop of the nose: terracotta stairs in the vent, a yellow-framed panel at the bonnet's front, terracotta panels round the 451 window, stairs on the bumper corners) and top.png (bonnet panels against the engine cover).

Every panel is now a filled shape with a 3-cell black gutter (was 2) in one of three strengths: solid terracotta with black linework, terracotta linework on a #6B3528 ground, and #6B3528 with black linework, so two inks and visible dim panels. Framed panels have a 2-cell frame and a 2-cell black ring inside it, setting them apart from the 1-cell linework (three line weights: gutter, frame, linework); panels too thin for a frame are toned blocks. Nose and tail panels carry yellow inner lines. Panels are larger (0.025-0.06 u², was 0.014-0.05) and the layout seed was chosen from six side by side. Evidence: sim 20261021-234724 top.png (separate framed triangles and nested chevrons over the roof, dim #6B3528 panels on the engine cover and rear deck, yellow inner lines on the tail haunches), side_l.png and side_r.png (framed panels with black gutters on the door and haunch, dim panels at the front fender and tail). The sides are only about 13 cells tall between the lower body and the window line, so their panels hold a frame, a ring and a short core, not the roof's full nesting.

24 marks now, in #DAD8CE on black, grouped: per side the lower-door row (Grivant, Huilec, Telvio), the duct behind the door in two rows (Ostrand, Rigmount, Hexmoor; Zentiq, Drexa above them, filling the black field under the light panel), and a column on the rear bumper behind the wheel (Norvane, Altmere); and two black plates on the bonnet's front corners with Brandvik and Hexmoor each. The sim's light panel sits in its own bracketed window, so the haunch's hot panel no longer breaks round a dark box. Evidence: sim 20261021-234724 side_r.png (crop of the tail: the duct's two rows, the rear-bumper column and the bracketed light panel), rear34.png (rear-bumper column) and front34.png (the bonnet-corner marks beside the headlights).

fixes.text: The sides are still the execution the owner flagged. The roof in top now shows SPIRIT's framed triangles and nested chevrons. But on the doors and haunch (side_l, side_r) the terracotta is thick, solid maze strokes with empty insides: no hatching, stepped diamonds or border rows inside the panels, and only one bright ink between the front fender and the tail. Each door and haunch panel should carry a visible inner pattern and a finer line weight at 10 m, like the roof does, so the sides read as framed panels and not as a labyrinth.

Behind the rear wheel on both sides (side_l, side_r, and rear34 under the 451), the lower mark in the rear-bumper column runs off the bumper's lower edge, so only half of it shows. Every mark in that column should sit whole on the visible face.

All 24 roster marks are small icon glyphs in one size. None of the roster's wordmarks appear, so at 10 m the sponsor groups (side_r under the 451 and in the duct, crop-nose on the bonnet corners) read as a row of symbols, not a raced car's sponsor layer. Mixing in a few small wordmarks per group would read more like a real race car.

orders.where: A is the better car. The front decides it. In front34 and crop-nose, A's bonnet, fender nose and bumper corner carry hot terracotta stair panels with yellow inner lines, so the nose is as strong as the tail, as the brief asks. B's nose is a dim #6B3528 fine weave around a plain black bonnet duct, which fails front-as-back again. The top view backs this up. A reads as SPIRIT-style framed panels of different sizes: nested stepped triangles on the roof, framed engine-cover panels, yellow corner brackets on the front fenders and rear haunches. B's top is one even, busy pixel maze from nose to wing, which is the "pattern as wallpaper" the brief bans. The sides go the same way. A has more layers: yellow brackets framing the light panel, yellow rear lines, and a fuller roster of marks behind the door. On side_l, B's lower door-to-haunch area is bare black with only three marks. B's one real strength is the raked terracotta band over the haunch on side_l, side_r and rear34. It reads as a single direction at distance more clearly than A's busier panels, but it doesn't make up for the weak front and the wallpaper top.

B is the better car, mostly because of the front and the top. In A the bonnet and nose are dark, with only faint dim stairs around the number window (crop-nose, front34), so it fails front-as-back again. B's bonnet has hot terracotta stair panels with yellow inner lines and small roster marks, and its nose looks as layered as its tail. On the top view B has the nested roof chevron and SPIRIT-style panels in different sizes. A's top is an even, directionless pixel print, the "wallpaper" the brief bans. On the haunches A leaves a large plain black field around the sim's light panel (side_r, side_l, rear34). B frames the light panel with yellow brackets, groups marks under it and runs yellow lines to the tail, which gives the yellow its share without crowding the number. A does one thing better: its side panels have a stronger raked lean, so the side_l and side_r distance images read as one direction. B's side panels are more upright and maze-like. That is A's only clear win and doesn't outweigh the plainer front and haunches. The beltline crops are about equal.
